category: EVENT ZERO — December 2025 Western Washington floods (AR sequence Dec 3–22, 2025; main flood Dec 8–12; second AR Dec 14–17; third Dec 18–21). All local times PST = UTC-8.
summary: Event Zero is well documented and reconstructable to the hour from primary sources. A three-AR sequence (Dec 3–5, Dec 7, Dec 8–11) culminated in a CW3E AR-4 (coastal WA) / AR-3 (Cascade foothills) atmospheric river with ~96 h of AR conditions, a second moisture pulse late Dec 9, snow levels near 9,000 ft during that pulse, and >10 in (locally 13–17 in; >24 in two-week totals) over the Olympics and Cascades onto soils saturated by the Dec 3–7 rains, with near-record-low snowpack so snowmelt was negligible. NWS Seattle issued a Hydrologic Outlook at 12:56 PM PST Thu Dec 4, the first Flood Watch at 4:10 PM PST Fri Dec 5 (effective 4 AM Mon Dec 8 through 4 PM Fri Dec 12, 14 counties), the first river Flood Warnings the afternoon/evening of Mon Dec 8 (Cowlitz, Puyallup/Orting, Skykomish, Snoqualmie, Snohomish, Concrete all at MAJOR), the Skagit-at-Mount-Vernon warning at 9:01 AM Tue Dec 9 (36.9 ft), and by 5:24 PM Dec 9 forecast crests above the 1990 record (41.5 ft MV; 47.4 ft Concrete), peaking at 42.3 ft on the 3:14 PM Wed Dec 10 statement, before being revised down (39.1 ft by 2:04 AM Dec 11; 38.26 ft later Dec 11) to an observed 37.73 ft at 12:15 AM PST Fri Dec 12 — a new record by 0.36 ft over Nov 25, 1990 (37.37 ft) despite a lower flow (~133,000 vs 152,000 cfs). A Flash Flood Watch for potential Skagit levee/dike failure was issued 7:13 PM Dec 10. Records (USGS/NWPS preliminary): Skagit nr Mount Vernon 37.73 ft; Snohomish at Snohomish 34.15 ft NWS (USGS IV 34.45 ft, 5:35 PM Dec 11) vs 33.5 ft 1990; Cedar at Renton 18.25 ft / 12,400 cfs at 3 PM Dec 11 vs 17.13 ft/10,600 cfs 1990; White River at R St 12,000–12,400 cfs / 117.07 ft Dec 15 (dam-release driven) vs 8,230 cfs 2022. Near-records: Skagit nr Concrete 41.0 ft/151,000 cfs (record 42.21 ft 2003); Snohomish nr Monroe 24.64 ft/115,000 cfs (record 25.3 ft 1990); Snoqualmie nr Carnation 60.76 ft/89,700 cfs (record stage 62.21 ft 2009, but highest flow in the top-5 list); Skykomish nr Gold Bar 24.01 ft/115,000 cfs (record 24.51 ft 2006); Nooksack at N. Cedarville 150.44–150.49 ft/67,300 cfs (called a record at the time over 149.6 ft, but NWPS now lists Nov 15, 2021 at 150.76 ft as official record — unresolved); Stillaguamish at Arlington ~20.2–20.9 ft (record 21.34 ft 2023). Puyallup at Puyallup peaked 44,400 cfs/28.67 ft (minor category) because Mud Mountain Dam stored ~70% of its flood pool (peak pool ~1,185 ft, 74,600 af, 8 PM Dec 12); Howard Hanson set a record pool (1,189.3 ft, 77,700 af, ~75%, 9 AM Dec 12) holding Green nr Auburn to 12,100 cfs (moderate); USACE took Section 7 control of Ross and Upper Baker on Dec 8 (Ross inflow ~50,000 cfs Dec 11 vs 450 cfs outflow; peak pool 1,594.53 ft 4 AM Dec 12) and again at 8:30 AM Dec 15, with a preliminary estimate of 4–5 ft of Skagit stage reduction. Levee events: Skagit floodwall held (seepage/boils; Cockerham Island breach; Sterling overflow; Gages Slough/Burlington flooded Dec 12 AM); Whatcom levees damaged at Mount Baker Rim, Twin View, Hovander Park, Glacier-Gallup; Ebey Island/Tualco overtopping Dec 10; Orting overtopping Dec 11; Desimone levee (Green River, Tukwila) breach ~11:30 AM Mon Dec 15 with a Flash Flood Warning at 11:51 AM; White River HESCO levee failure in Pacific ~1:20–1:39 AM Tue Dec 16. Evacuations: ~75,000–78,000 in Skagit County's 100-yr floodplain (Level 3 Mount Vernon 5:00 PM Dec 10; county-wide by ~8:19 PM); Sumas/Everson/Nooksack/Marietta/parts of Ferndale Dec 10; up to ~100,000 statewide at various times. Declarations: state Proclamation 25-07 on Dec 10 (2:14 PM), amended 25-07.1 Dec 16; FEMA EM-3629 Dec 12, 2025; FEMA DR-4906 April 7, 2026 (incident period Dec 5–19, 2025). One WA death (Dec 16, Snohomish). Post-event: CW3E event summary (Dec 23), UW OWSC analyses (Jan 13 & Feb 7, 2026), King County FCD flood-event report (Feb 2026), USACE damages-prevented analysis (Jul 20, 2026); no NWS service assessment or formal USGS peak-flow report was found. Best machine-readable sources for a hindcast: IEM AFOS archive of NWS Seattle products (exact issuance times and forecast crests), NWPS gauge API (flood categories + preliminary crest table), and USGS IV service (15-min provisional stage/flow).

evidence.claim: USACE Reservoir Control Center assumed Section 7 control of Ross Dam (Seattle City Light) and Upper Baker Dam (PSE) on Dec 8; Ross inflows peaked ~50,000 cfs Dec 11 while outflow was cut to a minimum of 450 cfs; Ross peak pool 1,594.53 ft at 4 AM Dec 12; USACE reassumed control 8:30 AM Dec 15 because natural flows were forecast to exceed 90,000 cfs at Concrete within eight hours; Concrete ~56,000 cfs on Dec 17; Mount Vernon 'record flood stage of over 37.7 feet'. (Release dated Dec 13, 2025.)

Howard A. Hanson Dam pool 1,189 ft (77,000 af, 74% of flood storage) at 9 AM Dec 12; Mud Mountain Dam peak pool ~1,185 ft (74,600 af, 70%) at 8 PM Dec 12; normal Green River flood-ops target 12,000 cfs at Auburn; White River ops release as fast as possible while keeping Puyallup at Puyallup below 50,000 cfs (release dated Dec 13, 2025).

July 20, 2026 preliminary analysis: Howard Hanson record pool 1,189.3 ft storing 77,700 af (~75% of flood storage), reduced Green River peak flow ~58% and stage >5 ft, ~$7.8B damages prevented; Mud Mountain used ~70% of storage, ~2 ft stage reduction through Puyallup, ~$215M; Section 7 reservoirs (Ross, Upper Baker, Wynoochee) ~$746M; total ~$8.7B; 'six atmospheric river pulses over nearly two weeks'.

KUOW (Dec 15) and OPB (Dec 16): USACE preliminary estimate that Skagit dam operations shaved 4–5 ft off the ~37-ft peak; Ross held back ~99% of inflow. Skagitonians (Feb 9, 2026) asserts 7–8 ft held back and ~45 ft without dams — unverified.

After the Dec 15 Desimone breach USACE cut Howard Hanson releases by 1,000 cfs (target had been 10,000 cfs at Auburn) and restored the 10,000-cfs target from noon Dec 16; reservoir down 26 ft from peak by Dec 16 (Auburn Reporter, Dec 17 1:45 PM). King County FCD report: after the Pacific HESCO breach USACE delayed Mud Mountain release increases and then stepped up by 500 cfs increments.

Snohomish PUD: Spada Lake rose 15 ft in two days and reached the Culmback Dam spillway by 6:50 PM Wed Dec 10; Jackson Hydroelectric Project run at full capacity to minimize spill; Sultan River rising from spillway discharge Dec 11.

Tolt Dam and Chester Morse/Masonry Dam (Seattle Public Utilities) flood operations: no quantitative releases found; Carnation reported SPU said Tolt Dam 'operating well within normal ranges'; SPU Dec 18 notice concerned Cedar River turbidity. Upper Baker (PSE) pool/outflow numbers not found.

providers.relevance_to_cascadia_papsukkal: Regulation dominated the Green, White/Puyallup and Skagit outcomes; a hindcast must represent Section 7 takeover (Dec 8 and Dec 15), near-zero Ross outflow, and record Howard Hanson/Mud Mountain storage to reproduce observed downstream stages.
